quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to use:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, you should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force your way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will make room for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering from a driveway or private road, yield to all traffic already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system allows dangerous fumes to enter the passenger compartment. Fix any exhaust leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a hospital with emergency services is to the right.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross them to turn into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. You may only cross them to turn or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, slow down and yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself by passing poor drivers in traffic.
Following the vehicle ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to get through traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid conflicts with aggressive, careless, or unsafe drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a collision.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop at an intersection. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly so traffic and pedestrians can get out of your way.
Must honk your horn so traffic and pedestrians know to give you room.
Must stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway and yield to any traffic or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. You must do this by law.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If the rain is too heavy, pull over and stop until it clears up.

questions.question: To prepare for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Scan the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on finding problems before you reach them. Look far ahead but also scan the entire road and the sides. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are properly filled.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct air pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: Passing is prohibited:

options.text: In a curve.
Within 100 feet of an intersection.
If your lane has a solid yellow centerline.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in curves, hills, or places where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic. Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, or railroad crossing. Do not pass if signs or road markings prohibit it or if a vehicle ahead has stopped for pedestrians.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A deaf person.
A person involved with a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: You must always let a blind person with a white cane or guide dog cross first. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone's blind spot. Speed up or slow down so the other driver can see your car.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers.
Drive using your parking lights.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or 500 feet behind another car. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming cars.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while you are driving?

options.text: Reach down and attempt to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.
Turn the engine off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. Pull over safely and turn off the engine.
